evidence.quote: Coupling these new data with previous $^{12}$CO(2-1) and radio continuum observations, we primarily aim at carrying out an analysis of the molecular gas physics and jet-CO interplay in this object.

findings_qualitative.value: CO(1-0), CO(2-1), and CO(3-2) show distinct spatial morphologies: CO(1-0) has a central gap, CO(2-1) has a ring-like structure, and CO(3-2) shows a full disc peaking towards the core, indicating higher excitation in the inner regions.

evidence.quote: As a result, also the gas morphology changes: a gap is observed at the centre of the CO(1-0) distribution, whereas the CO(2-1) and CO(3-2) lines shows a ring-like and full disc morphology, respectively.

findings_qualitative.value: Millimetre continuum up to 348 GHz shows the same compact core-double lobe structure as at 5 and 10 GHz and is dominated by non-thermal synchrotron emission with no clear evidence of thermal dust emission.

evidence.quote: The great morphological similarity between the continuum emission over this wide range of frequencies suggests that the continuum of NGC 3100 is dominated by non-thermal synchrotron emission from the core and extended radio structures up to at least 348 GHz.

findings_qualitative.value: HCO+(4-3) is tentatively detected at 5 sigma in an unresolved blob 2 arcsec west of the core at blueshifted velocities on the receding CO side, suggesting kinematic decoupling and jet-induced compression.

evidence.quote: Interestingly, HCO$^{+}$(4-3) emission is detected only at blueshifted velocities (see Section 4.2), while it is located in a small region of the receding (i.e. redshifted) CO side.
This suggests that the two molecular species have opposite velocity gradients (i.e. they are kinematically-decoupled) in that region.

findings_qualitative.value: SiO(3-2) and HNCO(6-5) shock tracers are undetected, which together with faint HCO+(4-3) may indicate a deficiency of very dense (n_crit > 10^6 cm^-3) cold gas in the inner regions.

evidence.quote: The SiO(3-2) and HNCO(6-5) shock tracers are undetected: this - along with the tentative HCO$^{+}$(4-3) detection - may be consistent with a deficiency of very dense (i.e. $n_{\rm crit} > 10^{6}$ cm$^{-3}$) cold gas in the central regions of NGC 3100.

claims.hypothesis: Expanding radio jets and lobes in the LERG NGC 3100 interact with the surrounding molecular gas, altering its excitation conditions.
claims.experiment: Create resolution-matched, spatially-resolved flux density ratio maps R_21 = S_CO(2-1)/S_CO(1-0) and R_31 = S_CO(3-2)/S_CO(1-0) and compare them spatially with 10 GHz JVLA radio continuum lobes.
claims.result: Two components are found: an outer low-excitation component (ratios ~1-4) and an inner high-excitation component spatially correlated with the radio lobes where R_21 >= 8 and R_31 >= 12, implying optically thin gas with T_ex >= 50 K.
claims.finding: The expanding radio plasma is driving a jet-ISM interaction that strongly alters the excitation conditions of the inner circumnuclear molecular gas.

evidence.quote: By comparing the relative strength of these three CO transitions, we find extreme gas excitation conditions (i.e. $T_{\rm ex}\gtrsim50$ K) in regions that are spatially correlated with the radio lobes, supporting the case for a jet-ISM interaction.

By making a spatial comparison between the regions where the highest line ratios are observed and the location of the radio lobes, it is clear that also in NGC 3100 the expanding radio plasma is likely responsible for such different gas conditions in the inner areas.

claims.hypothesis: Non-circular motions in the central molecular disc of NGC 3100 are driven by both a nuclear spiral perturbation and a radio jet-driven outflow that strongly perturbs the gas kinematics.
claims.experiment: Fit a 3D warped rotating disc + two-armed spiral model to the CO(3-2) cube using KinMS_MCMC, inspect velocity residuals along major and minor axes, and extract local spectra in residual regions A, B, C, and D.
claims.result: Bulk gas is in regular rotation, with two non-rotational components: major-axis inflow/outflow streaming motions (+90 and -250 km s^-1) at the spiral arms, and a minor-axis jet-driven outflow with v_max ~ 200 km s^-1, M_out = 5.6 x 10^4 M_sun, and M_dot <= 0.12 M_sun yr^-1.
claims.finding: Two non-circular components (spiral streaming and jet-induced outflow) are confirmed, but the jet-CO coupling only mildly affects the gas kinematics with negligible global impact, much weaker than predicted by simulations or seen in Seyfert-like jet-ISM systems.

evidence.quote: two distinct non-rotational kinematic components can be identified in the inner gas regions: one can be associated to inflow/outflow streaming motions induced by a two-armed spiral perturbation; the second one is consistent with a jet-induced outflow with $v_{\rm max}\approx 200$ km s$^{-1}$ and $\dot{M}\lesssim 0.12$ M$_{\odot}$ yr$^{-1}$.

These values indicate that the jet-CO coupling ongoing in NGC 3100 is only mildly affecting the gas kinematics, as opposed to what expected from existing simulations and other observational studies of (sub-)kpc scale jet-cold gas interactions.

claims.hypothesis: Jet-ISM interaction in NGC 3100 compresses the gas and drives shocks detectable in dense gas (HCO+(4-3)) and shock tracers (SiO(3-2), HNCO(6-5)).
claims.experiment: Image HCO+(4-3), SiO(3-2), and HNCO(6-5) data cubes at 105 km s^-1 channel width and map the HCO+(4-3)/CO(2-1) line ratio relative to the radio lobes.
claims.result: HCO+(4-3) is tentatively detected (5 sigma) adjacent to the base of the radio lobe with R_HCO up to ~0.7, while SiO(3-2) and HNCO(6-5) are undetected (< 0.15 mJy beam^-1).
claims.finding: The tentative HCO+(4-3) detection is consistent with localized jet-induced gas compression, while the non-detection of shock tracers and faintness of HCO+(4-3) suggest an intrinsic deficiency of very dense (n_crit > 10^6 cm^-3) gas.

evidence.quote: HCO$^{+}$(4-3) emission is tentatively detected in a small area adjacent to the base of the northern radio lobe, possibly tracing a region of jet-induced gas compression.

The SiO(3-2) and HNCO(6-5) shock tracers are undetected: this - along with the tentative HCO$^{+}$(4-3) detection - may be consistent with a deficiency of very dense (i.e. $n_{\rm crit} > 10^{6}$ cm$^{-3}$) cold gas in the central regions of NGC 3100.

claims.hypothesis: The cold gas and dust reservoir in NGC 3100 was externally accreted via galaxy interaction rather than internally generated by stellar mass loss or halo cooling.
claims.experiment: Compare the spatial distribution of CO(1-0) and optical B-I dust extinction, estimate dust mass in co-spatial regions, and compute the molecular gas-to-dust ratio and gas-phase metallicity.
claims.result: CO(1-0) and dust are tightly co-spatial in the central structure and eastern patch, with M_gas/M_dust = 560 (>= 200 across X_CO uncertainties) and sub-solar metallicity 12+log10(O/H) < 7.9.
claims.finding: The strongly sub-solar metallicity and dust-CO co-spatiality rule out internal stellar/cooling origin and confirm external accretion, likely from the gas-rich companion NGC 3095.

evidence.quote: By measuring the molecular gas-to-dust ratio in the regions where they are co-spatial, we estimate a strongly sub-solar gas-phase metallicity (i.e. $<7.9$).

These and other observational and theoretical constraints analysed in previous works strongly support an external origin of the cold ISM in NGC 3100, probably via interaction with the companion gas-rich star-forming galaxy NGC 3095.

why_this_data.value: Multiple CO transitions probe gas excitation temperature and density, HCO+(4-3) traces dense gas (n_crit > 10^4 cm^-3), SiO(3-2) traces fast shocks (v > 50 km s^-1), HNCO(6-5) traces slow shocks (v < 20 km s^-1), and NGC 3100 showed clear signs of jet-CO interaction in previous CO(2-1) and JVLA data.

evidence.quote: Higher-$J$ transitions require rapidly increasing densities and temperatures to be excited (i.e. $n_{\rm crit} \propto J^{3}$ and $T_{\rm ex} \propto J^{2}$; (cite: Bolatto13)), therefore ratios of multiple CO lines can be used to probe the excitation temperature and density of molecular gas
A multi-species approach is therefore key to properly characterise the impact of jet-induced feedback on the physics of the surrounding cold gas.

why_this_method.value: Natural weighting maximizes sensitivity to extended emission; masked moment maps recover flux while minimizing noise; 3D kinematic modelling with KinMS accounts for beam smearing and separates warps from non-circular motions; local spectral extraction avoids flux-weighting biases of moment 1 residual maps.

evidence.quote: All the continuum maps were made using natural weighting in order to maximise the sensitivity, with the goal of imaging extended emission from the radio source.
Full kinematic modelling is the only way to derive reliable estimates of the intrinsic gas velocity dispersion

Caution is needed, however, as interpreting the gas motions from the sole residual map may lead to draw inaccurate conclusions. This is because - by definition - the mean line-of-sight velocities are flux density-weighted and thus biased towards the brighter components.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Merger-induced shocks as the cause of enhanced HCO+ emission (rejected in favour of jet-induced gas compression due to spatial coincidence with the radio lobe base).

evidence.quote: Enhanced dense gas emission can be induced by various type of perturbations (such as merger-induced shocks; (cite: Konig18)). However, Figure 7 clearly shows that the faint HCO$^{+}$(4-3) emission arises from a region adjacent to the base of the southern radio lobe, making a jet-induced gas compression the most likely scenario.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Internal gas origin from stellar mass loss or hot halo cooling (rejected because freshly cooled gas is dustless and internally produced gas in ETGs has super-solar metallicity, whereas < 7.9 is measured).

evidence.loc: CO-dust comparison and gas-phase metallicity: implications for the gas origin
evidence.quote: Indeed, dusty cold gas produced through internal processes (i.e. stellar mass loss and/or hot halo cooling) in ETGs is expected to have a higher abundance of heavy elements (i.e. super-solar metallicities) than ISM acquired from outside the galaxy (cite: Martini13; Davis15).

limitations_admitted.value: Poor S/N at the very centre of the CO(3-2) distribution and in the redshifted excess of Region C prevents extracting reliable spectral features or performing Gaussian fits there.

evidence.quote: We note that we also attempted to extract the spectrum of the region at the centre of the gas distribution showing the brightest redshifted residuals, but the poor S/N ratio in that area does not allow to clearly distinguish any spectral feature and carry out a reliable analysis.
However, the S/N ratio of the corresponding channels is too low to allow a proper Gaussian fitting and thus robustly identifying it as an additional kinematic component.

limitations_admitted.value: Core continuum spectral index alpha_core has large fitting errors due to scatter across multi-epoch observations (possible core variability), and some thermal dust contribution to the unresolved core cannot be excluded.

evidence.quote: although we cannot exclude some contribution from this mechanism to the unresolved core emission.

The observed scatter in the data points, however, results in large fitting errors, making $\alpha_{\rm core}$ poorly constrained. Since the various flux measurements are taken at different epochs, we may be observing the effects of core variability.

limitations_admitted.value: HCO+(4-3) detection is only 5 sigma in 4 channels, too marginal for higher moment maps or firm conclusions without other dense/shock gas transitions.

evidence.quote: The significance of the detection is not sufficient to produce reliable higher moment maps (line emission can be identified only in four channels of the data cube, with a peak S/N $=5$; see Table 11 and Section 4.2).

This hypothesis, however, currently remains purely speculative, as observations of other HCO$^{+}$ transitions and/or of different dense/shocks gas tracers (such as HCN, HNC, CS, CH$_{3}$OH, etc. ) would be needed to draw more solid conclusions.

limitations_admitted.value: Spatially-resolved HI observations are not yet available, and X_CO is uncertain (especially at low metallicity), making the derived gas-phase metallicity an upper limit with systematic uncertainty.

evidence.quote: Spatially-resolved observations of the atomic hydrogen in NGC 3100 are currently not available. We thus estimate a *molecular* gas-to-dust mass ratio, which thus yields to an upper limit of the actual gas-phase metallicity.
Spatially-resolved observations of the atomic hydrogen in NGC 3100 are currently not available.

referee_caveats_inferred: Inconsistent text regarding the location of the HCO+(4-3) detection relative to the radio lobes: Section 4.4 states it is adjacent to the base of the southern radio lobe, whereas the Abstract, Section 5.2.2, and Summary state northern radio lobe.

Single-transition CO ratios (R_21, R_31) are interpreted using simple LTE optically thin approximations without non-LTE radiative transfer modelling (e.g., RADEX) to break temperature-density-optical depth degeneracies.
Outflow mass and rate rely on visually defined velocity channels (dark-grey shaded regions in Regions C and D) rather than multi-component spectral decomposition.
